questions.q: What problem does a CTE solve compared to deeply nested subqueries?
options: CTEs eliminate the need for JOIN entirely
CTEs can return more rows than subqueries can
CTEs are the only way to use WHERE inside a subquery
Readability — a CTE names a subquery instead of forcing you to track nested parentheses
questions.explain: WITH name AS (...) gives a subquery a name, making complex logic much easier to follow.

questions.q: In 'WITH ExpensiveProducts AS (...) SELECT ... FROM ExpensiveProducts', how is ExpensiveProducts used in the following query?
options: Exactly like a real table
It cannot be referenced again after being defined
As a column alias only
As a stored procedure
questions.explain: The CTE name is referenced in FROM just like any table or view name.

questions.q: Can the same CTE be referenced more than once in the statement that follows it?
options: Yes — useful when you need the same intermediate result compared against itself
Only when using GROUP BY
Only if it's wrapped in a subquery
No, each CTE can only be referenced exactly once
questions.explain: The CategoryAverages example references the same CTE twice — once aliased, once inside a scalar subquery.

questions.q: How long does a CTE remain usable?
options: It persists permanently in the database, like a table
For the entire session, until the connection closes
Only for the single statement immediately following its WITH clause
For 24 hours by default
questions.explain: CTEs are temporary and scoped to one statement — they are not saved or reusable across separate queries.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a CTE and a VIEW (covered in Lesson 58)?
options: There is no meaningful difference between them
A CTE is temporary and scoped to one statement; a VIEW is a genuinely reusable, saved named query
VIEWs are temporary; CTEs are permanently saved
A CTE can only be used with SELECT; a VIEW can only be used with INSERT
questions.explain: This distinction is explicitly previewed in this lesson as the reason to look forward to Lesson 58.
